root_idea.summary: Forceful forward movement that overcomes resistance or control.
root_idea.development: The root develops from a horse overpowering its rider into meanings of uncontrolled or heedless haste, while also producing specialized names for related objects and qualities.

senses.definition: To rush forward headlong, with energetic and uncontrolled momentum; to run wild.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction, it describes people hastening away so that nothing turns them back, evoking the motion of an ungovernable horse rather than ordinary speed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse: to overpower its rider, break loose, and run away so that it becomes ungovernable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The motion may include going at random without a fixed aim and resisting every attempt to turn it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be quick, swift, brisk, lively, or sprightly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an approved quality, contrasting with the refractory sense; the usage is also reported as obsolete except for possible figurative application to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a person or animal: to go heedlessly or at random, without consideration or a fixed aim, not following a guide; also, to hasten after someone or something so that nothing turns one back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This broader human or animal usage includes following one's natural desire without deliberation or guidance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a woman: to leave her usual dwelling in anger and go to her family without permission.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reported conventional use concerns leaving the husband's house before divorce.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a ship: to leave its course and become ungovernable by its sailors.
Of a desert: to lead a group far away because of its great extent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative description of the desert's effect on travelers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an object of desire: to baffle or thwart a person's efforts to attain it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The subject is the desired object, which defeats the attempt to reach it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A trick or act by which a beast overcomes its rider and runs away with him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term denotes the beast's characteristic act of becoming uncontrollable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A refractory horse or mare that overcomes its rider, runs away, and cannot be governed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective may describe an animal that will not bend its head or be turned from its course; in this sense it denotes a fault.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quick, swift, brisk, lively, or sprightly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In this sense the adjective describes an energetic quality that is not necessarily a fault.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person or animal that proceeds at random or heedlessly, follows natural desire without consideration or guidance, and is difficult to turn back.
Routed, defeated, or put to flight in warfare.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a plural usage referring to men.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A desert that leads travelers far away because of its great extent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The desert is likened to an uncontrollable horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small blunt-headed arrow used by boys for practice or play, sometimes bearing a date or clay on its head so that it does not wound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may be used to shoot at birds without killing them; the object is also called جُبَّاحٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A collective plant whose extremities bear soft, ear-like growths resembling fox-tails or the heads of certain grasses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The singular form is جُمَّاحَةٌ, and plural forms are جَمَامِيحُ or, in poetry, جَمَامِحُ.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence is an imperfect plural form, يَجْمَحُونَ; the public headword is normalized to the Form I perfect citation form جَمَحَ.
